Accident & Incident Investigation.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to investigate workplace accidents and incidents in a structured and legally compliant manner. The training focuses on identifying immediate and root causes, collecting and analysing evidence, interviewing witnesses, compiling investigation reports, and recommending corrective and preventive actions. Learners will be equipped to conduct effective investigations that support legal compliance, reduce repeat incidents, and improve workplace safety performance.
outline: Legal and compliance requirements for incident investigation
Definitions and classification of accidents, incidents, and near misses
Roles and responsibilities of investigators and employers
Incident reporting requirements and timelines
Evidence collection and scene preservation
Interviewing techniques and witness statements
Root cause analysis methods
Development of corrective and preventive actions
Incident investigation reporting and documentation
Monitoring effectiveness of corrective actions
outcomes: Explain legal requirements relating to accident and incident investigations
Collect and preserve evidence following an incident
Conduct structured interviews with witnesses
Identify immediate, underlying, and root causes of incidents
Compile investigation reports and recommend corrective actions
audience: Health and Safety Officers and Representatives
Accident & Incident Investigation.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive an Accredited Certificate aligned to Unit Standard 244288.

First Aid Level 3.us_name: Provide first aid in the workplace
First Aid Level 3.description: This accredited course provides learners with advanced knowledge and practical skills to provide first aid in the workplace. The training focuses on managing complex injuries and medical emergencies, advanced patient assessment, coordination during emergencies, and effective use of first aid equipment. Learners will be equipped to respond confidently to serious workplace incidents until professional medical assistance arrives.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for advanced first aid
Roles and responsibilities of a First Aider (Level 3)
Advanced assessment of casualties and emergency scenes
Advanced basic life support and CPR principles
Management of severe bleeding, shock, and trauma
Treatment of fractures, burns, and spinal injuries
Management of medical emergencies and unconscious casualties
Use and maintenance of advanced first aid equipment
Reporting, documentation, and handover to emergency services
outcomes: Conduct advanced assessments of emergency situations
Apply advanced first aid techniques for serious injuries
Manage medical emergencies and trauma effectively
Coordinate first aid responses during workplace incidents
Comply with workplace first aid and reporting requirements
audience: Employees responsible for workplace first aid
First Aid Level 3.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 120497.

Advanced OHS Act.description: This accredited course provides learners with in-depth knowledge and a detailed understanding of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, including its procedures, regulations, and practical application in the workplace. The training focuses on legal compliance, monitoring of control measures, recordkeeping requirements, and employer obligations related to training and communication. Learners will be equipped to interpret legislation, identify non-compliance, and support effective implementation of the OHS Act across workplace activities.
outline: Overview and purpose of the Occupational Health and Safety Act
Principles and structure of relevant health and safety legislation
Legal compliance requirements and regulatory obligations
Identification of deviations from legal and safety requirements
Control measures required to achieve and maintain compliance
Monitoring and review of health and safety control measures
Recordkeeping and documentation requirements
Employer obligations regarding training, instruction, and communication
Practical application of advanced OHS Act requirements
outcomes: Demonstrate in-depth knowledge and understanding of relevant OHS legislation
Explain legal requirements for compliance with the OHS Act and regulations
Identify deviations from safety plans and required control measures
Monitor and review activities to ensure effectiveness of control measures
Demonstrate knowledge of legislative recordkeeping requirements
Explain the legal obligations of employers regarding training and communication
audience: Health and Safety Officers and Practitioners
Advanced OHS Act.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive an Accredited Certificate.
entry_requirements: Completion of the OHS Act (Basic) course or equivalent knowledge

Basic Rigging and Slinging.us_name: Perform basic rigging and slinging operations
Basic Rigging and Slinging.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to perform basic rigging and slinging operations safely in the workplace. The training focuses on identifying lifting hazards, selecting and inspecting lifting equipment, applying correct slinging techniques, and communicating effectively during lifting operations. Learners will be equipped to support safe lifting activities and comply with occupational health and safety requirements.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for rigging and slinging
Roles and responsibilities of rigging and slinging personnel
Hazard identification and risk assessment for lifting operations
Types of lifting equipment and slings
Inspection of slings, hooks, shackles, and lifting accessories
Safe slinging methods and load control
Load weight estimation and centre of gravity
Hand signals and communication during lifting operations
Safe work practices during lifting and moving of loads
outcomes: Identify hazards associated with rigging and slinging activities
Select and inspect appropriate lifting equipment
Apply correct slinging techniques for different loads
Communicate effectively during lifting operations
Perform basic rigging and slinging operations safely
Basic Rigging and Slinging.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 116229.

Asbestos Awareness.description: The Working with Asbestos Safety Course provides essential knowledge to identify asbestos, understand its health risks, and apply safe working practices where asbestos-containing materials (ACMs) may be present. The course focuses on awareness, legal compliance, exposure control, and safe work procedures for workers who may encounter asbestos during maintenance, renovation, demolition, or construction activities.
outcomes: Understand health risks associated with asbestos exposure
Identify materials that may contain asbestos
Use asbestos registers and exposure records correctly
Apply safe work practices when working near asbestos
Understand legal duties, prohibitions, and licensing controls
Respond appropriately when asbestos is suspected or identified
audience: Construction and maintenance workers, plumbers, electricians, technicians, supervisors, facility maintenance staff, contractors working on older buildings, Safety Officers, and SHE Representatives.
entry_requirements: Basic literacy and numeracy. No prior asbestos training required.
Asbestos Awareness.certification: Learners who successfully complete the course will receive a Certificate of Attendance for the Working with Asbestos Safety Course.

Basic Fire Awareness.description: This accredited course aims to provide learners with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to respond effectively to fire emergencies in the workplace. The training covers fire prevention principles, correct response procedures, and the safe use of firefighting and emergency equipment. Learners will be equipped to fight containable fires, retreat safely when required, and hand over incidents to appropriate emergency personnel to enhance survival and reduce damage during fire emergencies.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for fire safety
Procedures for dealing with fires
Fire chemistry, types of fire, and fire classifications
Selection of appropriate firefighting procedures
Identifying, selecting, and checking firefighting and safety equipment
Fighting containable and extinguishable fires
Procedures for retreating safely from a fire site
Fire handover procedures to appropriate personnel
Reporting and recording the status of fires and firefighting equipment
outcomes: Explain procedures for dealing with workplace fires
Identify different types of fires and select appropriate firefighting methods
Inspect and use firefighting equipment correctly
Safely fight containable fires
Retreat safely when conditions become unsafe
Hand over fire incidents to emergency personnel
Report and record fire incidents and equipment status
Basic Fire Awareness.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 12484.

Basic Firefighting.description: This accredited course enables learners to acquire the knowledge and practical skills required to identify potential causes of fires, prevent workplace fires, understand fire detection methods, and apply emergency firefighting procedures. The training focuses on fire preparedness, correct response to fire emergencies, and the safe operation of firefighting equipment. Learners will be equipped to respond effectively to fire incidents while ensuring personal safety and workplace compliance.
outline: Basic knowledge pertaining to fires and fire behaviour
Causes of workplace fires and fire prevention measures
Fire detection systems and methods
Fire preparedness methods and emergency procedures
Roles and responsibilities during fire emergencies
Selection and use of appropriate firefighting methods
Operating firefighting equipment safely
Safe firefighting techniques for containable fires
Emergency response, evacuation support, and reporting
outcomes: Explain basic fire behaviour and fire principles
Identify causes of workplace fires and apply prevention measures
Recognise fire detection methods and warning systems
Apply fire preparedness and emergency response procedures
Operate firefighting equipment safely and effectively
Basic Firefighting.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 120331.

First Aid Level 1.us_name: Provide first aid as an advanced first responder
First Aid Level 1.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to provide basic first aid treatment in the workplace. The training focuses on assessing emergency situations, performing basic life support, treating common injuries and illnesses, and maintaining first aid equipment. Learners will be equipped to respond confidently and effectively to medical emergencies until professional medical assistance arrives.
outline: Legal requirements and responsibilities of a first aider
Principles of first aid and scene safety
Primary and secondary casualty assessment
Basic life support (CPR awareness and recovery position)
Management of bleeding, wounds, and shock
Treatment of burns, fractures, and soft tissue injuries
Medical emergencies such as fainting, seizures, and choking
Use and care of first aid equipment and kits
Recording and reporting of first aid incidents
outcomes: Assess emergency situations and ensure scene safety
Provide basic first aid treatment for common injuries
Perform basic life support procedures
Manage bleeding, shock, and medical emergencies
Maintain first aid equipment and complete incident records
First Aid Level 1.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 119567.

Basic Plumbing Skills Course.description: This course prepares learners for entry into the plumbing industry and forms the foundation toward becoming a qualified plumber at NQF Level 2, once sufficient workplace practical experience has been obtained.
outline: Introduction to plumbing principles and the plumbing industry
Health, safety, and basic plumbing legislation
Plumbing tools, equipment, and materials
Pipe types, fittings, and joining methods
Domestic cold and hot water supply systems
Basic installation and maintenance of geysers
Installation and maintenance of toilets, basins, and showers
Drainage systems and basic waste removal principles
Reading and interpreting basic plumbing diagrams
Pipe measurement, layout, and simple calculations
Fault finding and common household plumbing problems
Good housekeeping and professional work practices
outcomes: Understand basic plumbing principles and terminology
Identify and correctly use common plumbing tools and materials
Install and maintain basic domestic plumbing components
Perform basic plumbing maintenance tasks safely
Read basic plumbing drawings and layouts
Apply safe work practices in plumbing environments
audience: School leavers seeking a skilled trade
Individuals with no prior plumbing experience
Career changers looking for a stable trade
Individuals planning to start a plumbing business in the future
Basic Plumbing Skills Course.certification: Progression toward NQF Level 2 plumber status requires additional practical workplace experience in line with industry requirements.

outcomes: Learners will be able to:
Identify hazards and apply risk control measures
Understand legal health and safety responsibilities
Perform the statutory duties of a SHE Representative
Investigate incidents and recommend corrective actions
Respond safely to fire emergencies
audience: Safety Officers, Supervisors, Managers, SHE Representatives, and employees requiring multi-skill safety compliance training across construction, manufacturing, logistics, and industry.
entry_requirements: Basic literacy and numeracy. No prior safety training required.
BIG 5 SAFETY COMBO.certification: Learners found competent will receive Accredited Certificates for each unit standard successfully completed.

Breathing Apparatus.us_name: Use and maintain self-contained breathing apparatus
Breathing Apparatus.description: This course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to safely use and maintain breathing apparatus in hazardous or oxygen-deficient environments. The training focuses on understanding atmospheric hazards, correct donning and doffing procedures, equipment inspection, safe operation, and emergency procedures. Learners will be equipped to use breathing apparatus correctly while complying with occupational health and safety requirements.
outline: Legal and compliance requirements for breathing apparatus use
Types of breathing apparatus and their applications
Atmospheric hazards and oxygen-deficient environments
Roles and responsibilities of breathing apparatus users
Pre-use inspections and equipment checks
Donning, operation, and doffing procedures
Limitations and duration of breathing apparatus
Maintenance, cleaning, and storage requirements
Emergency procedures and user safety considerations
outcomes: Identify hazardous atmospheres requiring breathing apparatus
Inspect breathing apparatus and identify defects
Correctly don, operate, and remove breathing apparatus
Understand equipment limitations and safe working durations
Apply emergency procedures while using breathing apparatus
Breathing Apparatus.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive a Statement of Results aligned to the relevant Unit Standard.
entry_requirements: Medically fit to use breathing apparatus

Cherry Picker Operator.us_name: Operate a self-propelled elevating work platform
Cherry Picker Operator.description: This course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to safely operate a cherry picker in accordance with occupational health and safety legislation and workplace procedures. The training focuses on pre-use inspections, safe operating techniques, hazard identification, emergency procedures, and shutdown requirements. Learners will be equipped to operate cherry pickers safely in construction, maintenance, warehousing, and industrial environments.
outline: Legal and compliance requirements for MEWP operation
Types and applications of cherry pickers
Roles and responsibilities of a cherry picker operator
Hazard identification and risk assessment
Pre-use inspections and equipment checks
Safe operating procedures and load limitations
Working at heights and fall protection requirements
Emergency procedures and rescue awareness
Shutdown, parking, and post-operation procedures.
outcomes: Identify hazards associated with cherry picker operations
Conduct pre-use inspections and identify defects
Operate a cherry picker safely and correctly
Apply safe working at heights practices
Respond appropriately to emergency situations

COIDA – Compensation for Occupational In.us_name: Explain compensation for occupational injuries and diseases
COIDA – Compensation for Occupational In.description: This accredited course provides learners with a clear understanding of the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) and its application in the workplace. The training focuses on employer and employee responsibilities, reporting of injuries and diseases, compensation claims processes, and the management of occupational injury cases. Learners will be equipped to ensure compliance with COIDA requirements and support effective injury management and compensation administration.
outline: Purpose and scope of the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act
Roles and responsibilities of employers and employees
Types of occupational injuries and diseases
Reporting procedures for workplace injuries and incidents
Compensation claims process and required documentation
Employer registration and assessments
Duties of the Compensation Commissioner
Managing return-to-work and rehabilitation processes
Consequences of non-compliance with COIDA
outcomes: Explain the purpose and requirements of COIDA
Identify employer and employee responsibilities under COIDA
Apply correct reporting procedures for occupational injuries and diseases
Understand the compensation claims process
Support compliance and effective injury management in the workplace
audience: Health and Safety Officers and Representatives
Administrators responsible for injury reporting and claims
COIDA – Compensation for Occupational In.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive an Accredited Certificate aligned to Unit Standard 259638.

Cold Water Supply Systems.us_name: Install, maintain and test cold water supply systems
Cold Water Supply Systems.description: Learners will be equipped to ensure cold water systems operate safely, efficiently, and in accordance with regulatory requirements.
outline: Principles of cold water supply systems
Types of cold water systems and components
Health, safety, and environmental requirements
Interpreting drawings, layouts, and specifications
System layout, pipe sizing, and material selection
Installation of cold water supply systems
Valves, fittings, meters, and backflow prevention
Pressure control and leak prevention
Testing and commissioning procedures
Fault finding and corrective actions
Routine maintenance and servicing
System isolation and shutdown procedures
Compliance with applicable standards and regulations
Documentation, inspection records, and handover procedures
outcomes: Identify components and types of cold water supply systems
Install cold water supply systems safely and correctly
Test and commission cold water systems
Perform routine maintenance and servicing
Identify and rectify common system faults
Comply with health, safety, and regulatory requirements
audience: Technicians involved in water supply systems
Individuals entering the plumbing or building services sector
entry_requirements: Basic plumbing knowledge or experience is recommended
Cold Water Supply Systems.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to SAQA Unit Standard 244507.

outline: Legislative and compliance requirements for confined space work
Definition and classification of confined spaces
Hazard identification and risk assessment in confined spaces
Safe entry procedures and permit-to-work systems
Personal protective equipment and safety equipment requirements
Atmospheric hazards and monitoring awareness
Emergency preparedness and response procedures
outcomes: Identify confined spaces and associated hazards in the workplace
Apply safe work procedures for confined space entry
Understand permit-to-work requirements and entry controls
Use and inspect basic personal protective equipment correctly
Respond appropriately to emergencies related to confined space work.

outline: Legislative and compliance requirements for confined space rescue
Roles and responsibilities of a confined space rescue team
Hazard identification and risk assessment during rescue operations
Rescue planning and permit-to-work considerations
Confined space rescue equipment and systems
Safe entry, retrieval, and casualty handling techniques
Communication, coordination, and teamwork during rescue operations
Emergency response procedures and post-rescue actions
outcomes: Identify hazards associated with confined space rescue operations
Understand the roles and responsibilities within a rescue team
Apply safe rescue procedures and emergency response techniques
Use confined space rescue equipment correctly and safely
Participate effectively in confined space rescue operations

Construction Site Supervision.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to effectively supervise construction site activities in compliance with occupational health and safety legislation, construction regulations, and project requirements. The training focuses on site supervision principles, planning and coordination of work activities, health and safety compliance, quality control, communication, and workforce management. Learners will be equipped to oversee construction operations, manage site risks, and ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and to required standards.
outline: Roles and responsibilities of a construction site supervisor
Legal and regulatory requirements for construction site supervision
Planning, organising, and coordinating construction activities
Health and safety management on construction sites
Hazard identification and risk assessment
Monitoring work progress, quality, and productivity
Supervising contractors and subcontractors
Communication, leadership, and conflict management
Incident reporting, investigations, and corrective actions
Record keeping, site documentation, and reporting
outcomes: Explain the role and responsibilities of a construction site supervisor
Apply legal and health and safety requirements on a construction site
Plan and coordinate daily construction activities
Monitor work quality, progress, and compliance
Supervise teams and contractors effectively
Construction Site Supervision.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive an Accredited Certificate aligned to Unit Standard 13964.

Controlling Hazardous & Dangerous Goods.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical understanding required to control hazardous and dangerous goods in the workplace. The training focuses on identifying hazardous substances, applying control measures, safe handling and storage practices, emergency response actions, and compliance with occupational health and safety requirements. Learners will be equipped to minimise risks to people, property, and the environment when working with hazardous and dangerous goods.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for hazardous and dangerous goods
Classification of hazardous and dangerous substances
Hazard identification and risk assessment
Control measures for hazardous and dangerous goods
Safe handling, storage, and segregation practices
Labelling systems and Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
Personal protective equipment requirements
Emergency response procedures for spills, leaks, and exposure
Reporting incidents and maintaining records
outcomes: Identify hazardous and dangerous goods in the workplace
Apply appropriate control measures to manage risks
Handle and store hazardous substances safely
Interpret labels and Safety Data Sheets
Respond effectively to hazardous substance emergencies
Support compliance with health and safety requirements
Controlling Hazardous & Dangerous Goods.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 244073.

Convey Dangerous Goods by Road (Drivers).description: This accredited course provides drivers with the knowledge and understanding required to safely convey dangerous goods by road in compliance with legal and safety requirements. The training focuses on classification of dangerous goods, vehicle and load safety, documentation, emergency procedures, and driver responsibilities. Learners will be equipped to transport dangerous goods safely while minimising risks to people, property, and the environment.
outline: Legal requirements for conveying dangerous goods by road
Classification of dangerous goods
Roles and responsibilities of drivers
Packaging, labelling, and placarding requirements
Vehicle safety and load securing
Documentation and transport instructions
Emergency procedures and incident response
Reporting accidents and dangerous goods incidents
outcomes: Identify different classes of dangerous goods
Apply legal requirements for transporting dangerous goods
Ensure vehicle and load safety compliance
Respond appropriately to dangerous goods emergencies
Comply with driver responsibilities and reporting requirements
audience: Drivers transporting dangerous goods by road
Supervisors responsible for dangerous goods transport
Employees involved in loading and transport operations
entry_requirements: Medically fit to operate a motor vehicle
Convey Dangerous Goods by Road (Drivers).certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 123259.

Cut-Off Saw Operator Safety.us_name: Select, use and care for power tools
Cut-Off Saw Operator Safety.description: Learners will gain an understanding of how to use cut-off saws safely, reduce the risk of injury, and comply with workplace safety requirements when cutting materials such as pipes, metal, masonry, and concrete.
outline: Cut-off saw safety legislation
Legal requirements under the Occupational Health and Safety Act
Main components and structure of cut-off saws
Safety precautions for cut-off saw operators
Safety precautions related to the machine and work environment
Safe operating procedures for rotary and handheld cut-off saws
Operational maintenance of cut-off saws
Mounting and checking abrasive wheels
Refuelling procedures and fuel safety
Checking spark plugs and air filters
Basic adjustments and safe storage of equipment
Hazard identification and risk control measures
outcomes: Identify legal and safety requirements for cut-off saw operation
Identify components and controls of a cut-off saw
Operate a cut-off saw safely and correctly
Perform basic operational maintenance and inspections
Apply hazard controls and safe working practices
Comply with workplace safety requirements when using cut-off saws
audience: Cut-off saw and power tool operators
Cut-Off Saw Operator Safety.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to SAQA Unit Standard 10255.

Drainage & Rainwater Systems Installatio.us_name: Install, maintain and test below ground drainage systems
Drainage & Rainwater Systems Installatio.description: This course is ideal for learners progressing in plumbing, drainage, or water management roles.
outline: Principles of drainage and rainwater management systems
Health, safety, and environmental requirements
Interpreting drawings, layouts, and site plans
Below-ground drainage system components and materials
Excavation, trenching, bedding, and backfilling practices
Pipe laying techniques, gradients, and jointing methods
Inspection chambers, gullies, and access points
Testing and commissioning of drainage systems
Fault finding and corrective actions for drainage systems
Rainwater harvesting and stormwater control principles
Installation of gutters, downpipes, and rainwater outlets
Rainwater discharge, diversion, and drainage connections
Testing and maintenance of rainwater systems
Compliance with applicable standards and regulations
Documentation, inspections, and handover procedures
outcomes: Install and maintain below-ground drainage systems
Test drainage systems for compliance and performance
Install and maintain rainwater collection and discharge systems
Identify faults and carry out corrective actions
Apply safe work practices during excavation and installation
Comply with plumbing and drainage regulations
entry_requirements: Basic plumbing knowledge or experience is recommended
Medically fit for excavation and installation work
Drainage & Rainwater Systems Installatio.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to SAQA Unit Standards 244498 and 244495.

Fall Arrest Techniques.us_name: Explain and perform fall arrest techniques when working at height
Fall Arrest Techniques.description: This course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to safely use fall arrest systems when working at heights. The training focuses on hazard identification, selection and inspection of fall arrest equipment, correct anchoring techniques, safe use of harness systems, and emergency response awareness. Learners will be equipped to apply fall arrest techniques correctly to prevent falls and reduce the risk of serious injury or fatality.
outline: Legal and compliance requirements for fall arrest systems
Principles of fall protection and fall arrest
Roles and responsibilities of users and employers
Hazard identification and risk assessment for working at heights
Types of fall arrest systems and components
Inspection, care, and storage of fall arrest equipment
Correct fitting and use of full body harnesses
Anchorage points and connection methods
Safe working practices while using fall arrest systems
Emergency response and rescue awareness.
outcomes: Identify fall hazards associated with working at heights
Select appropriate fall arrest systems for specific tasks
Inspect fall arrest equipment and identify defects
Fit and use fall arrest equipment correctly
Apply safe work practices when working at heights.

Fall Protection Plan Development.us_name: Assess a worksite for work at height and prepare a fall protection plan
Fall Protection Plan Development.description: This course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to develop, implement, and review a fall protection plan in accordance with occupational health and safety legislation and construction regulations. The training focuses on identifying fall hazards, conducting risk assessments, selecting appropriate fall protection measures, and documenting control measures. Learners will be equipped to compile compliant fall protection plans for construction, maintenance, and industrial work environments.
outline: Legal and regulatory requirements for fall protection plans
Purpose and scope of a fall protection plan
Roles and responsibilities of employers, supervisors, and employees
Hazard identification and risk assessment for work at heights
Selection of fall prevention and fall arrest control measures
Identification of suitable anchorage points and systems
Emergency and rescue planning considerations
Documentation, implementation, and communication of the plan
Monitoring, review, and updating of fall protection plans.
outcomes: Interpret legal requirements relating to fall protection planning
Identify fall hazards and assess associated risks
Develop a compliant fall protection plan
Select appropriate fall prevention and fall arrest measures
Review and update fall protection plans to ensure ongoing compliance.

Fall Rescue.us_name: Install, use and perform basic rescues from fall arrest systems and implement the fall protection plan
Fall Rescue.description: This course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to perform safe and effective fall rescue operations following a fall arrest incident. The training focuses on rescue planning, hazard identification, correct use of rescue equipment, casualty handling, and coordination of rescue activities. Learners will be equipped to respond promptly to fall emergencies while minimising further risk to the casualty and rescue team.
outline: Legal and compliance requirements for fall rescue
Principles of fall arrest and suspension trauma
Roles and responsibilities during fall rescue operations
Hazard identification and risk assessment for rescue activities
Rescue planning and selection of rescue methods
Fall rescue equipment and system setup
Casualty recovery and controlled descent techniques
Communication and coordination during rescue
Emergency response procedures and post-rescue actions.
outcomes: Identify hazards associated with fall rescue operations
Understand the risks of suspension trauma and emergency response needs
Select and use fall rescue equipment correctly
Perform basic fall rescue techniques safely
Participate effectively in fall rescue operations

Fire Equipment Inspector.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to inspect firefighting equipment in the workplace to ensure it is safe, compliant, and operational. The training focuses on identifying different types of firefighting equipment, conducting routine inspections, recognising defects, maintaining inspection records, and reporting non-compliance. Learners will be equipped to support workplace fire safety and ensure firefighting equipment is ready for use during emergencies.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for firefighting equipment inspection
Types and uses of firefighting equipment
Roles and responsibilities of a fire equipment inspector
Inspection criteria for fire extinguishers and related equipment
Identifying defects, damage, and non-compliance
Tagging, labelling, and inspection intervals
Recordkeeping and inspection registers
Reporting defects and corrective actions
Storage and accessibility requirements for firefighting equipment
outcomes: Identify different types of firefighting equipment
Inspect firefighting equipment for defects and compliance
Complete inspection tags and inspection records
Report faulty or non-compliant equipment
Support workplace fire safety compliance
audience: Employees responsible for fire safety equipment
Fire Equipment Inspector.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 259584.

Fire Marshal.us_name: Demonstrate knowledge of fire prevention and firefighting equipment
Fire Marshal.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical understanding required to perform the duties of a Fire Marshal (Fire Warden) in the workplace. The training focuses on fire prevention, identification of fire hazards, emergency procedures, evacuation coordination, and the correct use of firefighting equipment. Learners will be equipped to assist with fire emergencies, support safe evacuations, and promote fire safety compliance in the workplace.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for fire safety
Roles and responsibilities of a Fire Marshal
Fire chemistry and classes of fire
Fire hazard identification and prevention measures
Emergency procedures and evacuation coordination
Use and limitations of firefighting equipment
Fire alarms, signage, and emergency communication
Assisting occupants during emergencies
Post-incident procedures and reporting
outcomes: Explain the role and responsibilities of a Fire Marshal
Identify fire hazards and apply prevention measures
Assist with emergency evacuations
Use firefighting equipment safely and correctly
Support workplace fire safety and emergency procedures
Fire Marshal.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 259585.

Flagman (Traffic Controller).us_name: Apply flagging procedures to control traffic
Flagman (Traffic Controller).description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to safely control traffic using flagging procedures in work zones. The training focuses on traffic control principles, correct use of signage and hand signals, hazard identification, communication, and personal safety. Learners will be equipped to perform flagman duties safely and effectively in construction, roadworks, maintenance, and industrial environments.
outline: Legal and workplace requirements for traffic control
Roles and responsibilities of a flagman
Hazard identification and risk assessment in traffic control areas
Traffic control plans and work zone layouts
Use of flagging equipment, signs, and PPE
Correct hand signals and communication techniques
Managing vehicle and pedestrian movement
Emergency situations and incident response
Personal safety and situational awareness
outcomes: Explain the role and responsibilities of a flagman
Identify hazards associated with traffic control activities
Apply correct flagging procedures and hand signals
Control traffic safely and effectively
Comply with legal and workplace traffic control requirements
Flagman (Traffic Controller).certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to Unit Standard 242974.

General Machinery Regulations (GMRs).description: The course is designed to assist supervisors, managers, and appointed competent persons in ensuring legal compliance and promoting safe machinery operations within the workplace.
outline: The following topics will be covered during the course:
01. Overview of the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHS Act)
02. Understanding and interpreting occupational health and safety legislation
03. Occupational health and safety terminology and legal liabilities
04. Roles and responsibilities of competent persons overseeing machinery
05. Competency requirements for machinery supervision appointments
06. Appointment and responsibilities of assistants to machinery supervisors
07. Duties of manufacturers, designers, erectors, and installers
08. Importance of risk assessments, audits, and safe operating procedures
09. Permit systems and lock-out procedures
10. Legal requirements and practical application of the General Machinery Regulations (GMRs)
11. Procedures for appointing competent persons
12. Relationship between role players in occupational health and safety

Grinders Operator (Angle Grinder) Safety.us_name: Select, use and care for power tools
Grinders Operator (Angle Grinder) Safety.description: The training focuses on identifying grinder hazards, selecting correct discs, applying safe operating techniques, controlling grinder speed, complying with hot work requirements, and implementing effective hazard controls. Learners will be equipped to operate grinders safely, prevent injuries, and comply with workplace safety requirements and applicable legislation.
outline: Hazards associated with angle grinder use and potential consequences of unsafe operation
Understanding angle grinder equipment, limitations, and correct operating techniques
Selection and correct use of grinder discs (grit, diamond, wire, and wood discs)
Matching grinder speed to different materials and checking wheel speed compatibility
Safe operating procedures, PPE requirements, and protective clothing
Pre-use inspections, pre-start checks, and common-sense safety practices
Safe grinding techniques for different materials, including stone
Do’s and don’ts for grinder operators and unsafe practices to avoid
Identification of risks, hazard controls, and implementation of control measures
Hot work requirements, fire risks, fire watch procedures, and controlled grinding areas
outcomes: Identify hazards associated with angle grinder operations
Select and use correct grinder discs for specific tasks
Apply safe operating procedures and PPE requirements
Control grinder speed for different materials
Implement hazard controls and hot work safety measures
Operate angle grinders safely and compliantly
Grinders Operator (Angle Grinder) Safety.certification: Learners who are found competent will receive Accredited Certificates aligned to SAQA Unit Standard 10255.

Hand Tools Operator.us_name: Use and maintain hand tools on a construction site
Hand Tools Operator.description: This accredited course provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to safely use and maintain hand tools on a construction site. The training focuses on identifying common hand tools, selecting the correct tool for specific tasks, applying safe operating procedures, conducting pre-use inspections, and maintaining tools in good working condition. Learners will be equipped to work safely, reduce tool-related incidents, and comply with construction site safety requirements and applicable legislation.
outline: Identification of common hand tools used on construction sites
Correct selection of hand tools for specific tasks
